config.prompt: Summarize the main causes and consequences of the 2008 financial crisis in a few paragraphs.

reference.text: The 2008 financial crisis, also known as the global financial crisis, was a severe economic downturn that was triggered by a housing market bubble bursting in the United States. The crisis began in 2007 and lasted for several years, affecting not only the US but also many other countries around the world. The main causes of the crisis were: (1) excessive borrowing and lending, particularly in the subprime mortgage market, where lenders extended large amounts of credit to borrowers who were not able to afford their mortgage payments; (2) the securitization of these mortgages, which allowed banks to package and sell them to investors, creating a complex web of financial instruments that were difficult to value; (3) the failure of regulatory bodies to adequately supervise the financial industry, allowing risky practices to go unchecked; and (4) the global imbalances, such as the large trade deficits in the US and the large trade surpluses in countries like China, which contributed to the buildup of debt and the instability of the financial system. reference_repeat.text: The 2008 financial crisis, also known as the global financial crisis, was a severe economic downturn that was triggered by a housing market bubble bursting in the United States. The crisis led to a global recession, widespread job losses, and a significant decline in economic output. The main causes of the crisis were: (1) excessive borrowing and lending, particularly in the subprime mortgage market, which led to a housing market bubble; (2) the securitization of these mortgages, which allowed banks to package and sell them to investors, creating a complex web of financial instruments; (3) the failure of regulatory bodies to monitor and regulate the financial sector; and (4) the excessive leverage and risk-taking by financial institutions, which made them vulnerable to collapse. The consequences of the crisis were severe, including: (1) a global recession, with GDP declining by 2.2% in 2009; (2) widespread job losses, with over 8 million jobs lost in the United States alone; (3) a significant decline in economic output, with the US GDP declining by 5.1% in 2009; and (4) a massive bailout of the financial sector, with the US government spending over $700 billion to rescue struggling banks
